free_tier.stated: no free tier; the entry shared plan is 'WAWs-1 ... EUR 5.93 month'

retention.stated: the disk persists while the plan is paid; the plan is billed hourly or monthly

egress.terms: 'Traffic ∞' and 'Network Up to 25 Gbps' on every plan

interface_detail: root SSH, the my.aeza.net panel, and an API
tooling: any SSH client; the vendor's API
chaining: a high-port, unlimited-traffic 2 GiB box in Europe; the cheapest unlimited-traffic row with a modern CPU, but 2 GiB is the ceiling at this price

limits.value: shared CPU: 'Processor time is distributed between virtual machines'

binding_note: traffic is unlimited and the port is 25 Gbit/s, so the shared CPU allocation is the only thing that can throttle; the price still puts the row out.

identity_cost.detail: an account and a payment method at order

reliability_note: no reliability event observed; the vendor's wiki describes a separate class of 'promo plans' aimed at new customers, which are not listed on this page
confidence_note: shapes and both prices for all five shared plans are quoted from the vendor's own plan list read today.

notes: EUR 5.93 is USD 6.64, so even the smallest Aéza plan misses the line, and 4 GB is EUR 11.87. The row is recorded because unlimited traffic on a 25 Gbit/s port with one IPv4 and a /48 of IPv6 is the most generous network term. Aéza's wiki advertises separate 'promo plans' for new customers; they were not listed on this page and are the one place a sub-USD-5 Aéza shape could hide.
